glosses: disguise, costume (outfit worn to hide one's identity)

examples.text: Le dernier type est le "cheval-jupon", un terme que l'ethnologue réserve à un déguisement pour une personne, constitué comme suit : le corps de la personne est entouré à la taille par un tissu — le jupon — recouvrant l'essentiel de ses jambes, une tête du cheval en bois[…]
examples.translation: The last type is the "hobby horse", a term which Ethnologue reserves for a disguise for a person, made as follows: the body of the person is surrounded at the waist by a cloth — the skirt — covering most of his legs; a horse's head of wood […]

glosses: Material (such as clothing, makeup, a wig) used to alter one’s visual appearance in order to hide one's identity or assume another.

examples.text: A cape and moustache completed his disguise.

glosses: The appearance of something on the outside which masks what’s beneath.
The act or state of disguising, notably as a ploy.

examples.text: Any disguise may expose soldiers to be deemed enemy spies.

glosses: A change of behaviour resulting from intoxication, drunkenness.
To change the appearance of (a person or thing) so as to hide, or to assume an identity.

examples.text: Spies often disguise themselves.
Bunyan was forced to disguise himself as a wagoner.

The official Central News agency said a Nationalist patrol boat Dec. 28 captured six Communist spies disguised as fishermen as they approached within 1,000 yards of the Paichuan in a motorized fishing craft. They were taken to Matsu for questioning.

glosses: To transform or disfigure, to change the appearance of in general.
To avoid giving away or revealing (something secret); to hide by a false appearance.

examples.text: He disguised his true intentions.

glosses: To dress in newfangled or showy clothing, to deck out in new fashions.
To dissemble, to talk or act falsely while concealing one’s thoughts.
To affect or change by liquor; to intoxicate.

examples.text: But my lord was angry, and being disguised with liquor too, he would not let him go till they played more; and play they did, and the luck still went the same way; […]
I have just left the right worshipful, and his myrmidons, about a sneaker or five gallons; the whole magistracy was pretty well disguised before I gave them the slip.

examples.text: Trotz Verkleidung habe ihn alle schnell erkannt.

glosses: Umhüllung zum Schutz vor Außeneinflüssen

examples.text: Die nachträgliche Verkleidung schützt gegen Wetterschäden.
„Mit fahrigen Fingern tastet er die Verkleidung unter dem Fenster ab, schnappt nach dem Türhebel, klappt und zerrt daran, rüttelt mit beiden Händen an der Tür.“
Um unseren Flur zu verschönern, bekam der Heizkörper eine Verkleidung.
„Da gibt es Falltüren im Fußboden, Gegengifte, Verkleidungen, und alles geht wild durcheinander, rennt und entwirrt sich, ohne dem Leser eine Minute Zeit zum Nachdenken zu lassen.“
